promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 10 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: A strong, sensible first week. Next week stays at three runs with small nudges in time, not daily running, because recovery days are what let a new runner's legs adapt.

flags.title: Calf tightness after runs
flags.detail: it cleared by morning, so keep gentle calf raises on Friday and ease into each run.

flags.title: Urge to add days
flags.detail: three runs plus dog walks is the right dose for now; adding a fourth day this early is where new-runner niggles start.

flags.title: Volume jump
flags.detail: moving from 0 to 3 runs is a big step, so we grow by minutes, not extra days.

answers.question: I want to be ready for the 5K in November. Should I run every day next week to get there faster?
answers.answer: No, please do not run every day yet. Your legs, tendons and feet adapt on the rest days, not on the run days, and daily running this early is the fastest way to a calf or shin problem that costs you the race. Three run mornings, a light strength and walk day, and real rest days will get you to Nov 15 ready to run the whole way. We will grow the time on feet and the length of your running intervals week by week, and that is what turns a walk-runner into a 5K runner.

new.analysis:
Great first week on the board. Three sessions, every one finished pain-free with heart rate sitting in easy territory and a felt score of 6 or 7. That is exactly the shape I want in these first weeks: short, steady, and repeatable.

The plan for the week of Aug 31 – Sep 6 keeps your three run mornings and nudges each one up by a couple of minutes. A new runner's gains come from doing the same small thing a few more times, not from chasing distance. With 10 weeks until the 5K, we have time to grow slowly and arrive healthy.

I have added a rest day between every run and a gentle strength and walk day on Friday. The calf raises and squats on Friday will help the calf tightness you noticed the day after runs. The dog walks the rest of the week count as recovery, not training, so keep enjoying them.

One thing to watch: tempting as it is to add a fourth run, more days are how brand-new runners pick up shin or calf trouble. Keep the three-day rhythm for a few more weeks, and I will bring in a longer Saturday walk-run and slightly longer running intervals as your legs show they are ready.

safetyCallouts.title: New calf or shin pain.
safetyCallouts.body: Mild tightness that clears by morning is normal early on, but sharp pain, pain that worsens run to run, or pain while walking means stop and see a physio before the next run.
